value.body: A welding engineer decides how metal parts will be welded — the process, filler, settings and checks — and makes sure the welds meet the required codes. Heavy fabrication shops, pressure-vessel and boiler makers, pipeline and EPC contractors, shipyards and railway and defence suppliers hire them. A day mixes shop-floor or site checks, inspection records and procedure paperwork.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech in Metallurgical, Materials or Mechanical

items.label: Common codes
items.value: ASME Section IX, AWS D1.1, API 1104

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers join fabrication, EPC and inspection companies as graduate engineers or QA/QC trainees through campus or direct hiring. Inspection certifications such as AWS CWI or CSWIP become important as you move into inspector roles.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Welding processes and metallurgy of welds
Visual inspection and reading NDT reports
Working to codes and client specifications

value.title: At a glance
items: Project and site work can mean travel and postings at remote sites.
Common next roles: senior welding engineer, QA/QC lead, third-party inspector.
Many international projects use the same codes, so the skills travel across countries.
